title: Nomenclature doesn't match domain
author: johns10

comments.body: I agree 100%. I have enhanced the code in the latest build allowing the [McpTool] attribute to be used on methods instead of the class, which now no longer requires a special attribute. The [McpFunction] attribute is maintained for compatibility but will be marked as deprecated once the documentation is updated. MCPSever.RegisterTool<T>() will also be deprecated in favor of MCPServer.Register<T>(), which should be functionally identical but semantically clearer. Thanks for bringing this to my attention

title: Support dynamically building MCP server
author: johns10

comments.body: I actually intended to expose the tool registration method. I agree that a programmatic API is needed, so if you have a working solution I'd be happy to look at your PR

I do and it is working with a sample project. I'm trying to get it integrated with my actual application to make sure it's sane. My first pass missed the mark wide. 

I may have to make a few mods to make tests run on my Mac. I'll try to keep it cross platform.

I'm having a really hard time understanding your distinction between McpTool and McpFunction ... I don't think there's actually such a thing as an McpFunction? I'm not sure it's the correct abstraction. Can you help me understand the rationale behind this?

Yeah I think your tool abstraction should be renamed to McpContainer (or something) and McpFunction should be renamed to McpTool. RegisterTool should be RegisterContainer. It makes this rather confusing to work in due to the mismatch between the library and the spec.

The rationale is that it was an oversight in early development, and nobody has brought it up as a point of confusion until now. And yes, that redundant call is a bug. Neither of these things are relevant to the issue you opened, so if you would like to open an issue about the Attributes feel free, just make sure to double check and remove any part of your LLMs response before you post it.

I've been through this a couple of times now ... my first 2 tries weren't able to support the same functionality. First attempt was passing dictionaries so there would have been no chance to maintain state on the class. The second one ... I missed the nomenclature difference between McpTool and McpFunction and was just trying to register functions.

This time I'm going to try taking a fluent builder approach.
I'm gonna go ahead and close this, as it looks like this added functionality matches the suggested feature. Thanks again for helping out, if you have any more issues reach out
Thanks for resolving do quickly and getting things cleaned up. Code looks much tighter. Will take another stab today.
